correctness.rationale: The dodecagonal norm is given explicitly by its six unoriented facet directions. Every admissible unit equilateral pair lies in a face of the compact 4-dimensional polytope determined by one tight signed facet for x, one for y, and one for x-y. The exact Q(sqrt(3)) certificate exhausts all 1728 such triples: 168 presentations are nonempty, of which 144 are points and 24 are segments, with 24 distinct endpoints. Both output norms equal sqrt(3) at every endpoint. On each segment, a common signed facet of x+y and a common signed facet of 2x-y attain sqrt(3) at both endpoints, so affinity gives the lower bound throughout, while convexity of the norm gives the matching upper bound. This proves the pointwise continuum claim, not merely a sampled or vertex-only statement.
risks: The face exhaustion is finite but nontrivial; its critical algebraic counts and supporting-facet checks are delegated to the bundled exact checker and were replayed successfully.
The result is for the stated facet normalization of a regular dodecagon; invariance under linear isometry is standard and no stronger affine-class statement is asserted.

value.rationale: The regular dodecagon is a canonical non-Hilbert polyhedral normed plane, while the defining paper singles out the value 6 and the two lengths sqrt(3) as the Hilbert-space behavior of G_L. The result shows that this canonical non-Hilbert space reproduces the Hilbert derived lengths for every admissible unit equilateral pair, not merely at one extremizer. This gives a sharp structural boundary for what G_L can detect and disproves any converse inference from the Hilbert value alone. The facet-face argument is also a reusable exact method for other polygonal equilateral-triangle constants.
risks: The finding is a canonical counterexample/benchmark rather than a classification of all polygonal norms.
